body.statement: Let \(P\) be homogeneous of degree \(r\geq1\). If \(G_P(X)\succeq0\) for every \(X\in C3\), \(\det G_P\equiv0\) in \(\mathbb R[S3]\), and \(\operatorname{rank}G_P(X_0)=2\) for some \(X_0\in C3\), then there exists \(u\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(G_P(X)u=0\) identically on \(S3\). Consequently, after a linear change of coordinates, \(P\) is a polynomial in one \(2\times2\) symmetric compression of \(X\).
body.justification: The three-dimensional theorem is retained as the direct specialization used by the complete denominator classification.
body.gap: The operative determinant is that of the trace-pairing symmetric-gradient matrix, not a coordinate Hessian; the new all-dimensional theorem supplies the applicable rigidity result.
body.consumer: The complete \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) denominator classification applies this specialization to the signed mixed residue.
body.proof_tex:
Apply the all-dimensional positive-gradient kernel-rigidity theorem with \(d=3\), \(S_d=S3\), and \(C_d=C3\).  The present hypotheses say respectively that \(P\) is homogeneous of degree \(r\geq1\), that \(G_P\) is positive semidefinite on \(C3\), that \(\det G_P\equiv0\), and that \(G_P\) has rank \(3-1=2\) at \(X_0\in C3\).  The all-dimensional theorem consequently supplies \(u\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}\) with
\[
 G_P(X)u=0
\]
identically on \(S3\).  Its compression conclusion says, after an orthogonal change of coordinates sending the last coordinate vector to a multiple of \(u\), that \(P\) depends only on the symmetric compression to \(u^\perp\).  Since \(\dim u^\perp=2\), this is exactly one \(2\times2\) symmetric compression, as claimed.
